findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an AC: CHANGELOG.md has `## [0.15.1] - YYYY-MM-DD` with the temperature fix under `### Fixed`, releases/fixVersions/RELEASE_DELTA/SCHEMA_VERSION 6 under `### Added`, and a `[0.15.1]: .../compare/v0.15.0...v0.15.1` footer.
evidence: "promote `## [Unreleased]` ... with hand-curated entries (the sampling fix under Fixed; releases/fixVersions under Added) and the compare footer link"
No AC mentions CHANGELOG.md.
findings.finding: The CHANGELOG work has no covering criterion, although the version-number justification depends on it ('The CHANGELOG entry lists those additions so the patch number does not hide them'). Nothing checks that `## [0.15.1]` exists with the fix under Fixed, releases/fixVersions under Added, and the compare footer link.
scenarios: The Added section is omitted; users upgrading a patch get SCHEMA_VERSION 6 and new commands with no notice.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an AC that the bug's fix commit is an ancestor of the v0.15.1 tag (e.g. `git merge-base --is-ancestor <fix-sha> v0.15.1`) and that the bug ticket is closed before step 3.
evidence: "after the bug's fix has merged on main and the bug is closed"
No AC references the fix commit or the bug ticket status.
findings.finding: No acceptance criterion proves the release actually contains the tapestried-oversize-blackfly fix. That fix is the stated purpose of the release, yet the plan only names its merge as a precondition ('after the bug's fix has merged on main and the bug is closed'). Every AC could pass for a 0.15.1 built without the fix.
scenarios: Release is dispatched before the fix's Gerrit change submits; 0.15.1 ships still sending `temperature` to Opus/Sonnet 5.
findings.suggested_fix: Record the fix's merge SHA in a comment. Add: `git fetch --tags && git merge-base --is-ancestor <fix-sha> v0.15.1` exits 0. Gate step 3 on the bug ticket being closed.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an AC proving the fix commit is in the release: record the fix's merge SHA and assert `git merge-base --is-ancestor <fix-sha> v0.15.1`, plus confirm the CHANGELOG Fixed entry references the bug.
evidence: "needs to reach users"
"after the bug's fix has merged on main and the bug is closed"
All six ACs assert version presence only (PyPI info.version, gh release view, registry search, Formula sdist).
findings.finding: The plan's headline intent is to get the temperature fix to users, but no acceptance criterion proves the released 0.15.1 actually contains that fix. Every AC checks only that version 0.15.1 exists on each channel. The precondition 'after the bug's fix has merged on main and the bug is closed' is stated in Approach but never verified against the release commit.
scenarios: The fix change is still in Gerrit review, or was reverted, when the bump is cut from origin/main. 0.15.1 publishes everywhere and every AC goes green, yet users still get Bedrock 400s.
findings.suggested_fix: Add AC: "Fix for tapestried-oversize-blackfly is an ancestor of the v0.15.1 tag (`git merge-base --is-ancestor <fix-merge-sha> v0.15.1` exits 0; SHA recorded in a comment)."

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] In Approach step 1, run `make changelog VERSION=v0.15.1` (git-cliff 2.13.1) to generate the 0.15.1 section from the commits since v0.15.0, then hand-curate it, since `[Unreleased]` is currently empty.
evidence: Plan: "promote `## [Unreleased]` in `CHANGELOG.md` to `## [0.15.1] - <date>` with hand-curated entries"
CHANGELOG.md:11 `## [Unreleased]` followed immediately by line 13 `## [0.15.0] - 2026-11-09`: the section is empty

docs/releasing.md:351-356: "if `[Unreleased]` already holds hand-curated entries, you can skip `make changelog` and simply retitle ... make changelog VERSION=vX.Y.Z   # prepends the [X.Y.Z] section from unreleased commits"
findings.finding: The plan says to 'promote `## [Unreleased]` ... with hand-curated entries'. That phrasing assumes the section already holds curated entries. It is empty in CHANGELOG.md (line 11 is followed directly by `## [0.15.0] - 2026-11-09`). docs/releasing.md §1a allows the retitle shortcut only 'if `[Unreleased]` already holds hand-curated entries'. Otherwise it requires `make changelog VERSION=vX.Y.Z` and then curating the generated section, so 'follow docs/releasing.md exactly' means running git-cliff here.
scenarios: The executor retitles an empty [Unreleased] and writes entries from memory. Fixes or features from the other commits since v0.15.0 that are neither the sampling fix nor releases/fixVersions get left out.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the CHANGELOG clause with: "`make changelog VERSION=v0.15.1` (git-cliff==2.13.1) to prepend the section from the commits since v0.15.0, then hand-curate it (the sampling fix under Fixed; releases/fixVersions under Added) and confirm the `[0.15.1]` compare footer link".

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an AC that `git rev-list -n1 v0.15.1` equals the recorded merge SHA, and dispatch only when origin/main HEAD equals that SHA.
evidence: "gh workflow run release.yml --ref main -f version=0.15.1"
AC 1 records the merge SHA but no AC compares it to the tag.
findings.finding: The plan dispatches release.yml with `--ref main` but never asserts that the released tag points at the reviewed version-bump merge SHA. If other changes land on main between Submit and dispatch, unreviewed commits ship in 0.15.1.
scenarios: A concurrent Gerrit submit lands on main after the bump commit and before `gh workflow run`.
findings.suggested_fix: Before step 3, check that `git ls-remote origin refs/heads/main` equals the merge SHA. Add AC: `test "$(git rev-list -n1 v0.15.1)" = "<merge-sha>"`.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify step 4 fully: get RUN from `gh run list --workflow release.yml -L1 --json databaseId`, get the env id from `GET .../runs/$RUN/pending_deployments`, and POST `{"environment_ids":[ID],"state":"approved","comment":"release 0.15.1"}`.
evidence: "with a JSON `--input` body (`environment_ids` integer array)"
findings.finding: Step 4's pending_deployments body is incomplete. GitHub's 'Review pending deployments' API requires `environment_ids`, `state` ("approved") and `comment`, but the plan specifies only `environment_ids`. The plan also does not say where `$RUN` and the environment id come from.
scenarios: The POST returns 422 and the executor stalls; or the executor guesses the environment id.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Make the Homebrew AC decode the content and anchor on the sdist URL, e.g. `gh api .../contents/Formula/rebar.rb --jq .content | base64 -d | grep -E 'url ".*nava_rebar-0\.15\.1\.tar\.gz"'`.
evidence: "`Formula/rebar.rb` ... points at the 0.15.1 sdist (`gh api repos/navapbc/homebrew-rebar/contents/Formula/rebar.rb`)"
findings.finding: The Homebrew AC's proving command cannot be read as written. `gh api .../contents/Formula/rebar.rb` returns base64-encoded `content`, so checking that it 'points at the 0.15.1 sdist' requires decoding first. The command also does not check the sha256.
scenarios: The executor greps the raw JSON for '0.15.1', which is base64, and gets a false negative or a false pass.
findings.suggested_fix: `gh api repos/navapbc/homebrew-rebar/contents/Formula/rebar.rb --jq .content | base64 -d | grep -E 'url "[^"]*nava_rebar-0\.15\.1\.tar\.gz"'`, and check that the formula's sha256 matches the PyPI sdist's `digests.sha256`.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Replace the prose checks with structured asserts: `gh api repos/navapbc/rebar/releases/latest --jq .tag_name` == v0.15.1; `jq -e '.info.version=="0.15.1"'` for PyPI; `jq -e` on `.servers[]` filtered by name=="io.github.navapbc/rebar" with version=="0.15.1".
evidence: "`gh release view v0.15.1 --repo navapbc/rebar` exists, marked Latest"
"lists version 0.15.1"
findings.finding: The GitHub Release AC requires 'marked Latest', but `gh release view` does not expose Latest status. The MCP Registry and PyPI ACs match on prose ('lists version 0.15.1', 'reports info.version 0.15.1') instead of a structured `jq -e` assertion. The MCP search can return multiple servers or versions, so a plain substring match can falsely pass.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria — GitHub Release / MCP Registry / PyPI
scenarios: 0.15.1 is published but not Latest and the check still passes.
The registry lists 0.15.10 or another server and a grep for '0.15.1' matches it.
findings.suggested_fix: PyPI: `curl -s https://pypi.org/pypi/nava-rebar/json | jq -e '.info.version=="0.15.1"'`. GitHub: `test "$(gh api repos/navapbc/rebar/releases/latest --jq .tag_name)" = v0.15.1` plus `gh release view v0.15.1 --json assets --jq '.assets[].name'` showing a .whl and a .tar.gz. MCP: `curl -s ... | jq -e '[.servers[] | (.server // .) | select(.name=="io.github.navapbc/rebar" and .version=="0.15.1")] | length > 0'`.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Before step 3, add a probe: install nava-rebar==0.15.0 and replay a store containing a RELEASE_DELTA / schema-6 event; confirm it is ignored, not rejected. If it is rejected, bump to 0.16.0 instead.
evidence: "`SCHEMA_VERSION` 5→6 for the additive `RELEASE_DELTA` event"
"The event schema row says new event types are additive and preserved-and-ignored by older clients"
findings.finding: The plan asserts that the SCHEMA_VERSION 5→6 bump is safe in a patch because new events are 'preserved-and-ignored by older clients', but nothing checks this. Patch upgrades are auto-adopted by `~=0.15.0` pins, and users who downgrade to 0.15.0 after writing RELEASE_DELTA events depend on this tolerance. If the reducer refuses stores with a newer schema version, the patch is breaking.
scenarios: A user upgrades to 0.15.1, creates a release (RELEASE_DELTA), then rolls back to 0.15.0 and the reducer errors on the schema version.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a failure/back-out section: rerun only failed jobs (`gh run rerun $RUN --failed`) for post-PyPI channel failures; never re-dispatch a published version; for a bad release, `pypi yank 0.15.1` and roll forward to 0.15.2.
evidence: Step 5 only handles a missing Homebrew bump: "trigger ... autobump.yml ... if the tap has not bumped".
No mention of yank, job rerun, or 0.15.2 roll-forward.
findings.finding: There is no back-out or partial-failure plan for an irreversible publish. PyPI version numbers cannot be reused, and release.yml fans out to PyPI, the GitHub Release, the MCP Registry and Homebrew. The plan does not say what to do if a later channel fails after PyPI succeeds, or if 0.15.1 proves bad.
scenarios: The MCP Registry publish fails after PyPI upload.
A regression is found after publish.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State defaults: if the baseline diff touches anything beyond `__version__`, stop and file a ticket rather than committing it; trigger Homebrew autobump if the formula is not at 0.15.1 within N minutes after the GitHub Release.
evidence: "(only `__version__` changes in `tests/unit/api_surface_baseline.json`)"
"trigger `gh workflow run autobump.yml ...` if the tap has not bumped"
findings.finding: Two steps contain unhandled branches. Step 1 asserts that 'only `__version__` changes' in the API baseline, but gives no instruction if the diff shows more. Step 5's 'if the tap has not bumped' has no wait time or decision rule before triggering autobump.
scenarios: The releases feature left the baseline stale and the regen diff includes new symbols.
The executor triggers autobump immediately, racing the scheduled bump.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the partial-failure recovery for release.yml: per channel, whether to re-run a single job, publish manually, or (if PyPI already has a bad artifact) yank and cut 0.15.2, citing docs/releasing.md if it already covers this.
evidence: "gh workflow run release.yml --ref main -f version=0.15.1"
"Confirm every channel; trigger `gh workflow run autobump.yml --repo navapbc/homebrew-rebar` if the tap has not bumped."
There is no stated handling for a partial release.yml failure or for a re-run after PyPI upload.
findings.finding: The publish fans out to immutable or shared external records: the PyPI version, the GitHub Release/tag, the MCP Registry entry, and the Homebrew formula. The plan defines a recovery path only for Homebrew (manual autobump). It does not say what to do if release.yml fails after PyPI has accepted 0.15.1 but before the GitHub Release or MCP Registry publish. In that case, re-running the workflow with the same version would fail on PyPI's immutable re-upload, so the procedure is not idempotent under retry.
scenarios: The PyPI publish job succeeds, then the MCP Registry publish step fails. A naive re-run of release.yml aborts on the duplicate PyPI upload, leaving the registry stuck on 0.15.0 with no documented manual path.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reword 'new release CLI commands' in the plan and the CHANGELOG Added entry as the new `edit --add-release/--remove-release/--set-releases` flags and the `--release` list filter.
evidence: Plan: "optional `releases` / `fixVersions` keys ... and new release CLI commands"
src/rebar/_cli/_parsers/core/writes.py:167-169: parser.add_argument("--add-release"...), ("--remove-release"...), ("--set-releases"...)
src/rebar/_cli/_parsers/core/reads.py:74: "--release", help="filter to tickets in release <name> ..."
No `release` subcommand is registered under src/rebar/_cli/_parsers
findings.finding: The plan says the releases feature adds 'new release CLI commands', and the CHANGELOG 'Added' entry is meant to describe it. The repo has no new command. The feature adds `--add-release` / `--remove-release` / `--set-releases` flags to `edit` (src/rebar/_cli/_parsers/core/writes.py:167-169) and a `--release` filter on a read command (src/rebar/_cli/_parsers/core/reads.py:74). docs/event-schema.md:47 likewise names `edit --add-release/--remove-release/--set-releases` as the emitter.
findings.location: Context / Problem (description of main since v0.15.0) → CHANGELOG Added entry
scenarios: The 0.15.1 CHANGELOG 'Added' entry announces release commands that users then cannot find in `rebar --help`.
findings.suggested_fix: Change "and new release CLI commands" to "and new `edit --add-release/--remove-release/--set-releases` flags plus a `--release` filter on listing".

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add docs/release-notes.md to Scope with a newest-first entry for RELEASE_DELTA / SCHEMA_VERSION 6 and the optional `releases`/`fixVersions` output keys, or state why the release commit leaves it out (e.g. a separate ticket owns it).
evidence: Plan Scope: "`pyproject.toml`, `server.json`, `uv.lock`, `CHANGELOG.md`, `tests/unit/api_surface_baseline.json`." docs/release-notes.md is not listed.
CHANGELOG.md:8-9: "Agent-visible contract changes live in [docs/release-notes.md](docs/release-notes.md)."
docs/release-notes.md:3-9: "This file tracks agent-visible *contract* changes (event/schema/API) ... called out here when they could be observed by an agent or a different rebar version."
docs/releasing.md §1a: "(Agent-visible *contract* changes stay in `docs/release-notes.md`.)"
search_files for 'RELEASE_DELTA' and 'fixVersions' in docs/release-notes.md returns no matches. RELEASE_DELTA is documented only in docs/event-schema.md, docs/ticket-model.md and ADR 0124.
Plan Context: "`SCHEMA_VERSION` 5→6 for the additive `RELEASE_DELTA` event ... optional `releases` / `fixVersions` keys in `ticket_state` / `jira_snapshot_entry` schemas"
findings.finding: The plan's Scope leaves out docs/release-notes.md, even though the release ships agent-visible contract changes that the repo says must be recorded there. Those changes are the event-schema v6 (RELEASE_DELTA) and the optional `releases`/`fixVersions` keys in the ticket_state and jira_snapshot_entry output schemas. docs/release-notes.md has no entry for any of them today.
scenarios: An agent or an older-version clone reads docs/release-notes.md to learn about contract changes since 0.15.0. It finds nothing about the new RELEASE_DELTA event type, the schema v6 bump, or the new output keys. Yet a mixed-version shared origin/tickets is exactly the case that file exists for.
The 0.15.1 CHANGELOG entry follows the preamble and sends readers to release-notes.md for contract details, but no such entry exists.
findings.suggested_fix: Add `docs/release-notes.md` to the Scope list. In Approach step 1, add a newest-first section such as "## Jira fix versions become `releases` (RELEASE_DELTA, event schema v6, ADR 0124)". It should say that older clones preserve and ignore the new event type, and that `ticket_state` and `jira_snapshot_entry` gain only the optional `releases` and `fixVersions` keys. Stage it with `git add` in the same release commit.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a docs/release-notes.md entry for the RELEASE_DELTA event / SCHEMA_VERSION 6 and the optional releases/fixVersions keys (noting that older clients ignore the event and that fsck warns), and add docs/release-notes.md to Scope, unless the releases feature change already added one before the bump.
evidence: docs/releasing.md:345-346: "(Agent-visible *contract* changes stay in `docs/release-notes.md`.)"
docs/release-notes.md:7-9: "contract changes are called out here when they could be observed by an agent or a different rebar version."
search for 'fixVersions' in docs/release-notes.md: (no matches)
src/rebar/reducer/_version.py:41-42: "# 6: RELEASE_DELTA event ... SCHEMA_VERSION = 6"
api-stability.md:26: older binaries ignore new event types "(and `fsck` WARNs when the store holds newer types)"
findings.finding: The plan relies on the CHANGELOG entry alone to disclose the contract additions shipping in this patch: the RELEASE_DELTA event, SCHEMA_VERSION 5→6, and the optional releases/fixVersions output keys. The project routes agent-visible event/schema changes to docs/release-notes.md, which has no entry for this, and the plan's Scope leaves that file out.
findings.location: Context / Problem ("The CHANGELOG entry lists those additions so the patch number does not hide them"); Scope
scenarios: A team member upgrades to 0.15.1 and writes RELEASE_DELTA events to the shared tickets branch. Peers still on 0.15.0 see fsck warnings and no releases data, and the contract changelog meant for exactly this mixed-version case has nothing explaining it.
An agent that checks docs/release-notes.md for schema changes before upgrading sees nothing and treats 0.15.1 as a pure bug-fix drop-in.
findings.suggested_fix: In Approach step 1, add: 'If docs/release-notes.md does not already describe RELEASE_DELTA / SCHEMA_VERSION 6 and the new optional releases/fixVersions keys, add a newest-first entry stating that 0.15.0 clients preserve-and-ignore RELEASE_DELTA and that their fsck WARNs on it.' Add docs/release-notes.md to Scope.
